title: The Wrong Drawer Is Killing Your Herbs
editorialNotes: No statistic. Shelf-life claims (2-3 weeks) are method guidance from the brief's Pillar 3 reference, not a cited study.

thread.element: herb sprig reviving in a glass of water
thread.endState: upright green sprig in a water jar

copy.headline: You bought fresh herbs Sunday. They were slime by Wednesday.
copy.body: It was never the herbs. It was the drawer.

copy.headline: The crisper drawer is built for vegetables - sealed, still, humid.
items: Cut herbs are not vegetables. They're cut stems.
Sealed in a bag, they suffocate and rot in days.

copy.headline: SOFT HERBS - treat them like flowers.
items: Basil, cilantro, parsley, mint, dill: trim the stems, stand them in an inch of water, loose bag over the top, into the fridge.

copy.headline: HARD HERBS - treat them like delicate laundry.
items: Rosemary, thyme, oregano, sage: wrap loosely in a slightly damp paper towel, then into a container or loose bag in the fridge.

copy.headline: One exception: basil hates the cold.
copy.body: Refrigerate basil and it blackens. Keep it on the counter in water, like a bouquet, away from direct sun.

copy.headline: Already wilting? Two rescues:
items: 1. Ice-water bath - limp greens and soft herbs perk back up in 15-30 minutes.
2. Blend the rest with olive oil, freeze in an ice-cube tray. Instant flavor bombs for months.

copy.headline: Your herbs weren't fragile. They were just in the wrong place.
copy.ctaLine: fond tells you what's about to turn - and how to store it before it does. Link in bio.
